anti_overlap: The historiography lens judges the record chain, attribution, and promises about record content; coordinate frames, resolution and datum mechanics belong to fd-geodetic-survey-network-order
It does not evaluate palettice API shape, crate placement, event-store performance, or Rust idiom — those belong to the core architecture, correctness and performance reviewers
It does not litigate whether the DF/Qud depth bet is worth making; it examines whether the artifact the goal demands could evidence the bet either way
Beads filing, commit/push discipline, and workspace test green are process items other reviewers own
decision_lens: For each sentence a player will read in the chronicle, ask which office wrote it — the engine's event log, the compiler's selection, or the grammar's voice — and whether a reader or a test could tell them apart afterwards. Then ask what this goal requires the record to contain that no honest compiler can promise in advance, and by what named mechanism that promise would be kept.
distance_rationale: A two-thousand-year bureaucratic craft for turning a daily unalterable record into a compiled, narrated history sits far outside software, simulation, or game design, yet it is the most refined body of practice that exists for the exact fork this goal leaves open: where the line runs between what happened, what was selected, and what was said about it. The bureau solved problems the goal states as open questions — a record whose subject may not read or edit it, an explicit rule that a house cannot compile its own history, judgment kept typographically separable from record, and structural forms (annals for chronology, treatises for institutions, biographies for persons) that keep a readable history queryable. Because its content is human archives rather than stars or engines, it cannot be pulled into critiquing the astrophysics; it can only test the goal's provenance and evidentiary structure.
expected_isomorphisms: Diaries of Activity and Repose (contemporaneous, unalterable) <-> the palettice event log as the immutable substrate of every historical claim
Veritable Records compiled from the diaries <-> the chronicle as selection and arrangement over the event log
Standard History with judgment and treatises <-> Qud-style grammar texture, names, gospels and flavor layered on top
The rule that a dynasty's history is compiled by its successor <-> who narrates a civilization that is still standing when the run ends
Interpolation (compiler's phrase reading as record) <-> chronicle prose asserting facts no event backs
Annal / treatise / biography division <-> chronology, institutions and persons as separately queryable views of one generated history
Direct writing (zhishu) as a professional norm <-> the 'every historical fact a real event through the engine' pole of the simulate/author fork
A commission asked to produce a history containing a required verdict <-> a DONE WHEN clause requiring the run to contain a fallen civilization
Archive gaps where the diarists lapsed <-> intervals the deferred-cascade settle mode resolves only at their boundary
focus: Whether the goal fixes a record chain — what counts as contemporaneous record (engine events), what counts as compilation (selection and arrangement into a chronicle), and what counts as narration (names, causes, gospels, flavor) — and whether each DONE WHEN artifact is attributable to a layer permitted to produce it, including the artifacts the goal requires the record to contain but a stochastic run cannot promise
name: fd-dynastic-historiography-record-chain
persona: Apply the perspective of a compiler in an imperial Bureau of Historiography — an official who served on the diarists' staff, edited a reign's Veritable Records, and sat on the commission compiling a fallen dynasty's standard history. They hold apart the daily record (contemporaneous, unalterable), the reign compilation (selected and arranged), and the narrated history (judgment, treatises, biographies). Of any statement they ask which office produced it, from which record, and what was cut.
review_areas: Whether the simulate/author question is really three (event production, selection and arrangement, naming and voice) rather than the GATE's binary-plus-hybrid, and which layer owns each
Whether 'at least one fallen civilization' is a promise a stochastic run can keep: guaranteed content needs a named mechanism (seed search, forced collapse, resampling), each proving something else
Whether 'evidenced by the event log itself' states an evidentiary standard — every chronicle statement derivable from events, with a check for interpolation (prose carrying facts no event backs)
Whether the chronicle's genre and reader are chosen: DF legends (exhaustive, queryable) and Qud histories (terse, selective) impose different completeness obligations and different costs
Whether deferred-cascade settle mode leaves gaps in the contemporaneous record, and whether the chronicle is permitted to date events inside an interval the engine only resolved at its boundary
Whether the project's own record chain holds — the dated brainstorm doc as the record of rulings (who ruled, on what rationale, what was rejected) rather than a summary later work cannot cite

severity_examples.condition: DONE WHEN requires 'one fallen civilization whose ruins/records are queryable in the present at a real location'. If the ratified seed's 120 centuries produce no fall, the only ways to close are to author the fall or to hunt seeds until one appears. Both change what the artifact proves, neither is named, and the choice will be made under turn pressure by whoever is at the keyboard. A record that must contain a given event is not a record — and this criterion is the whole evidence for the Reynolds layer.
severity_examples.scenario: The record is required to contain a specific event it may not produce

severity_examples.condition: GATE asks which layer owns names, gospels and flavor text, but DONE WHEN accepts 'a readable chronicle' with no requirement that statements be attributable to the events backing them. Once texture and record are interleaved in one text, no later test can separate compiler's voice from event, the 'evidenced by the event log itself' clause becomes unverifiable, and the depth bet the goal exists to test cannot be falsified by its own artifact.
severity_examples.scenario: Chronicle prose has no per-statement provenance, so interpolation is undetectable

severity_examples.condition: The goal cites DF legends and Qud histories together as its depth precedent and asks only for 'a chronicle a human can read'. Legends mode is an exhaustive, queryable record of every event; Qud histories are a terse selective narration over a much smaller substrate. The completeness obligation, the query surface, and the emitted volume differ by orders of magnitude, so the cost curve measured against the affordability envelope measures whichever genre was implicitly chosen.
severity_examples.scenario: The chronicle's genre is left unchosen while the cost curve depends on it

source_domain: Chinese imperial historiography and its bureaucratic record chain — Diaries of Activity and Repose (qijuzhu) into Veritable Records (shilu) into the Standard History (zhengshi), with the successor-dynasty compilation rule, the direct-writing norm, praise-and-blame judgment, and the annal/treatise/biography division of a compiled history
success_hints: Sort every DONE WHEN artifact into daily record, compilation, or narration; flag any artifact that spans two layers without saying which owns what
For each required historical fact, mark whether it is observed or guaranteed; a guaranteed fact must name the mechanism that guarantees it
List the statements a readable chronicle will need to make (why a civ fell, what a ruin is called, who a founder was) that no event in the log can supply, and ask who writes them
Ask what happens to a civilization still standing at the end of the run: who narrates it, in what tense, and whether the chronicle distinguishes concluded from ongoing
Check that the goal's own decision record meets the standard it imposes on the generated record: dated, attributed, rationale preserved, rejected options named
Test the OUT list under compilation pressure: readable prose demands names and causes, which is exactly the layer the GATE has not yet assigned
task_context: Target: a draft /goal condition for Mind State's stratified worldgen pipeline (one seed to galaxy scaffold to species stubs to civilizations of member Souls to a simulated deep history emitted as a readable chronicle), slice one on the measured palettice engine, written in an OUTCOME / GATE / DONE WHEN / OUT structure. Stress-test this draft goal (stratified worldgen at DF/Qud depth for Mind State, slice one on the palettice engine) before ratification: find missing forks, scope traps, wrong assumptions, and anything the GATE/DONE WHEN/OUT structure gets wrong. The goal is not yet ratified. Review the condition text as written — its forks, its acceptance criteria, and its exclusions — rather than the engine code.
